title: Food prices climb as conflicts and El Niño tighten grain supplies
gist: World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook (Oct 2026) projects its food price index up 10% in 2026 and 7% in 2027 (down 5% in 2028), driven by Black Sea attacks, dry weather and a very strong El Niño, with tight stocks-to-use (maize lowest since 2012-13, edible oils lowest since 2009-10) and biofuel demand; risks tilted to the upside, with a downside scenario surpassing 2022 levels.

insights.claim: The World Bank Group's food price index eased in October 2026 after a three-year high in September but stayed 15 percent above its year-earlier level.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
entities: World Bank Group food price index
insights.so_what: Food inflation momentum remains elevated year-on-year despite a monthly pause.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group's food price index eased

insights.claim: Grain prices surged 9 percent q/q in 2026Q3, with maize up 8 percent and wheat up 13 percent, driven by attacks on Black Sea shipping and ports, dry weather in major exporters and early effects of a very strong El Niño.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Long wheat/maize exposure is supported by geopolitical and weather supply shocks.
insights.quote: Grain prices surged 9 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q), driven by attacks on Black Sea shipping and ports
insights.locator: The World Bank Group's food price index eased

insights.claim: US wheat output is projected to drop 23 percent in 2026-27 to its lowest since 1970-71, Ukraine's exports to fall 18 percent, and global wheat output to decline 2 percent.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Wheat faces the strongest supply headwinds; watch US and Black Sea export flows.
insights.quote: U.S. output is projected to drop by 23 percent to its lowest since 1970–71
insights.locator: Global grain supplies are set to shrink

insights.claim: Global grain supply (production plus beginning stocks) is projected by USDA to fall about 20 million metric tons in 2026-27, the first decline in four years, though still the second highest on record, limiting upward price pressure.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Absolute supply remains ample, so price spikes depend on inventories and shocks rather than outright scarcity.
insights.locator: Global grain supplies are set to shrink

insights.claim: Global maize production is expected to fall 3 percent and rice 2 percent in 2026-27, with rice posting its first drop in a decade as El Niño weighs on Asian harvests.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Rice supply risk in Asia could trigger export restrictions; watch Asian rice exporters.
insights.quote: rice posting its first drop in a decade as El Niño weighs on Asian harvests
insights.locator: Global grain supplies are set to shrink

themes.theme: Edible oils squeezed by biofuel mandates

insights.claim: Global edible oil supply is projected to grow only 2.7 mmt in 2026-27 versus a long-term average annual increase of 5.7 mmt, partly due to the very strong El Niño.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Slower supply growth against rising demand supports vegetable oil prices.
insights.locator: Edible oil supply growth is slowing

insights.claim: Biofuel feedstock demand for soybean and palm oil is rising due to elevated energy prices, record U.S. biofuel volume requirements and Indonesia's increase of the palm oil share in biodiesel blends from 40 to 50 percent.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Energy-food linkage: higher crude and biofuel mandates transmit directly into vegetable oil prices; watch Indonesian B50 and US RVO policy.
insights.quote: Indonesia's increase in the palm oil share of biodiesel blends from 40 to 50 percent
insights.locator: Edible oil supply growth is slowing

insights.claim: The World Bank Group's oils and meals index was little changed in 2026Q3 q/q but remained 17 percent higher than a year earlier.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Vegetable oil complex stays structurally elevated.
insights.locator: Edible oil supply growth is slowing

insights.claim: The global maize stocks-to-use ratio is projected to fall to 21.5 percent in 2026-27, its lowest since 2012-13, though above the 2010-11 low of 13.2 percent; wheat and rice ratios edge down to 34 and 37.2 percent.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Low stocks raise price convexity to weather or trade shocks; favors upside optionality in grains.

insights.claim: The edible oils stocks-to-use ratio is set to fall to 12.5 percent, its lowest since 2009-10.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Tightest vegetable oil buffers in over 15 years make the complex highly shock-sensitive.

insights.claim: Tight inventory buffers could amplify the price effect of weather or trade shocks.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Expect higher volatility in agricultural futures.
insights.quote: These tight buffers could amplify the price effect of weather or trade shocks.

themes.theme: Food inflation and hunger in EMDEs

insights.claim: Median food price inflation in emerging market and developing economies rose to 3.9 percent y/y in 2026Q3 from 3.5 percent in 2026Q2, reaching 7.4 percent in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region and 122 percent in Iran.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Rising food inflation pressures EM central banks and import-dependent MENA sovereigns.
insights.quote: reached 122 percent in the Islamic Republic of Iran
insights.locator: Food price inflation is picking up

insights.claim: Severe food insecurity fell from 837 million people in 2021 to 779 million in 2025, aided by a 21 percent drop in global food commodity prices; with a projected cumulative 18 percent price rise in 2026-27 this tailwind becomes a headwind.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Reversal in food prices threatens social stability and fiscal subsidy costs in poorer importers.
insights.quote: that tailwind is set to become a headwind
insights.locator: Food price inflation is picking up

themes.theme: Forecast path and upside risk scenario

insights.claim: The World Bank projects its food price index to rise 10 percent in 2026 and 7 percent in 2027 before easing 5 percent in 2028, with grains up 14 and 9 percent and oils and meals up 17 and 8 percent in 2026 and 2027.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
entities: World Bank Group food price index
insights.so_what: Baseline implies a two-year food price upcycle peaking in 2027.
insights.locator: Food prices are set to keep rising

insights.claim: Upside price risks include stronger El Niño effects, prolonged Black Sea hostilities, export restrictions, higher energy prices and stronger biofuel demand.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Skew suggests owning upside protection in agricultural commodities.
insights.locator: Food prices are set to keep rising

insights.claim: Under a scenario of prolonged conflicts and stronger El Niño effects, the food price index would exceed the 2027 baseline by 12 percent and surpass its 2022 level.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Tail scenario would revisit 2022-style food crisis conditions with EM inflation and balance-of-payments stress.
insights.quote: the food price index would exceed the 2027 baseline by 12 percent and would also surpass its 2022 level
insights.locator: Food prices are set to keep rising
